title: Department of Energy: Phase 56J Continuation Decision
publisher: Department of Energy Office of Inspector General
summary: DOE OIG's FY 2025 evaluation concludes that FERC's unclassified cybersecurity program was effective and makes no recommendations, but the report explicitly concerns FERC as an independent agency within DOE. Phase 56J decision: Hold as a scope-exclusion decision and retain Partially Closed. The record is authoritative for FERC but cannot replace the selected department-wide DOE FISMA evaluation or department-level finding closure.
key_findings: Highest-value missing record: Department-wide FY 2025 FISMA evaluation or finding-level remediation.
Evidence state: Partially Closed to Partially Closed.
Continuation rule: Reopen when DOE OIG publishes the department-wide FY 2025 FISMA evaluation, a dated official status for that review, or finding-level remediation with department scope.
why_it_matters: The continuation decision tests a named next record against the selected denominator instead of expanding broad context or inferring performance from disclosure.
ftfn_relevance: Separates a new operating, program, or scope observation from complete closure.
Keeps evidence state separate from performance, safety, quality, readiness, value, and causation.
evidence_limits: FERC is an independent agency within DOE and has a distinct FISMA evaluation boundary. Its effective result cannot be generalized to the Department, laboratories, national security systems, incidents, recovery, or mission effects.
Department-wide FY 2025 FISMA evaluation, finding-level remediation, incidents, recovery, and laboratory or mission effects.
No causal effect, entity ranking, composite score, readiness score, or unsupported cross-entity comparison is supported.
